task_instance: Create a minimal Expo app, add expo-dev-client, configure eas.json with a development build profile, and build an Android development client locally with `eas build -p android --profile development --local` (the skill's core deliverable: producing an installable dev-client build).
blocker_detail: `eas build ... --local` (and the cloud equivalent) refuses to run without being logged into an Expo account: `An Expo user account is required to proceed. Either log in with eas login or set the EXPO_TOKEN environment variable`. This applies even to local builds, since eas-cli itself needs an authenticated Expo account/project association to run the build command at all. The sandbox's safety rules forbid using credentials/tokens or account-bound services, so this could not be worked around. Separately, even if login were allowed, a true local Android build also needs the Android SDK, and downloading it from dl.google.com was blocked by the outbound proxy (403 Forbidden) - a network_or_service_unavailable blocker. iOS builds additionally require Xcode/macOS, unavailable on this Linux runtime (missing_tool_in_runtime). All three build paths (EAS cloud, EAS local, and by extension any Android SDK based Gradle build) were blocked before a dev-client artifact could be produced.
evidence: Ran in /tmp/.../exec_ext/expo__skills__expo-dev-client/MyDevClientApp: (1) `npx --yes create-expo-app@latest MyDevClientApp --template blank` succeeded, scaffolding a working Expo project. (2) `npm install expo-dev-client` succeeded (package present in node_modules and package.json). (3) Wrote eas.json exactly matching the skill's documented development build profile (developmentClient: true, autoIncrement: true, appVersionSource: remote). (4) `npx --yes eas-cli --version` -> eas-cli/24.8.0 confirmed CLI is installable/runnable. (5) `npx eas-cli build -p android --profile development --local --non-interactive` failed immediately with 'An Expo user account is required to proceed. Either log in with eas login or set the EXPO_TOKEN environment variable' - i.e. even the local build path requires an authenticated Expo account, which the task's safety rules disallow. (6) `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://dl.google.com/android/repository/repository2-3.xml` returned a proxy CONNECT failure (403 Forbidden), showing the Android SDK (needed for a genuinely account-free local Gradle build) cannot be downloaded in this sandbox either. No dev-client .apk/.ipa was produced or verified.
